title: Loire Valley
description: France's longest river and its garden: crisp whites, fresh reds and every sweetness of Chenin.
L: Explain how climate changes along the river

The Loire is France's longest river, about 1,000 km. Vineyards line it for over 400 km, from the Atlantic near Nantes inland to Sancerre and Pouilly. The region is divided into four parts: the Pays Nantais, Anjou-Saumur, Touraine and the Central Vineyards. It's known as the garden of France.

Near the Atlantic, the Pays Nantais is maritime: mild and damp. Inland, through Anjou and Touraine, the climate becomes gradually more continental: warmer summers, colder winters. The Central Vineyards, near the centre of France, are continental. Throughout, the Loire is cool, keeping acidity high and alcohol moderate.
How does the climate change as you move up the Loire from the Atlantic?

The Loire was the playground of French kings in the Renaissance, who built châteaux like Chambord and Chenonceau. Many were built from tuffeau, a soft, white limestone. The caves dug to extract it now serve as cellars, especially in Saumur and Vouvray. The valley between Sully-sur-Loire and Chalonnes is a UNESCO site.
Which are parts of the Loire wine region?
The Loire has four parts along 400 km of river
The climate shifts from maritime to continental
Tuffeau built its châteaux and cellars
Link each grape to its area

Melon de Bourgogne makes Muscadet in the Pays Nantais. Chenin Blanc dominates Anjou and Touraine whites, dry to sweet. Cabernet Franc makes most of the reds, in Chinon, Bourgueil and Saumur-Champigny. Sauvignon Blanc leads the Central Vineyards and Touraine. Others include Gamay, Pinot Noir and Grolleau.

The Loire makes almost every style of wine: crisp dry whites, sweet botrytised whites, light reds, rosés, including Rosé d'Anjou, and sparkling wine, Crémant de Loire and Saumur. Cool climate and high acidity link them all. Chenin Blanc alone makes dry, sweet and sparkling.
Match each grape to its main area.
Each part of the Loire has its grape.
Most Loire wines are named after the place, not the grape. Learn the four grapes and their areas, and the labels open up.
The Loire makes only white wine.
Not true. It also makes reds, rosés and sparkling wines.
Melon, Chenin, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon lead the Loire
Each area has its own grape
Describe Anjou's whites and sweet wines

In the Pays Nantais, Muscadet is made from Melon de Bourgogne: light, crisp and saline. Muscadet Sèvre et Maine is the main appellation. Sur lie wines rest on their lees until bottling, gaining texture and a slight spritz. Since 2011, crus communaux, like Clisson and Gorges, show longer-aged, serious Muscadet.

Anjou makes Chenin Blanc in every style. Savennières, on schist, gives dry, powerful, long-lived whites. The Layon valley, with autumn mists, gives sweet botrytised wines: Coteaux du Layon, Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume, the Loire's first Grand Cru, in 2011. Anjou also makes rosés like Rosé d'Anjou and Cabernet d'Anjou.
Which Loire appellation became the first Grand Cru, in 2011?
Quarts de Chaume makes sweet, botrytised Chenin.

Saumur, with tuffeau soils and cellars, makes Saumur Brut, a traditional method sparkling wine, mainly from Chenin Blanc, and Saumur-Champigny, a fresh, fruity Cabernet Franc red. Many sparkling houses, like Bouvet-Ladubay and Gratien & Meyer, are based there, ageing wine in tuffeau caves.
Sancerre is in the Central Vineyards.
Muscadet is crisp Melon, often sur lie
Anjou makes dry Savennières and sweet Layon Chenin
Saumur makes sparkling wine and Cabernet Franc reds

Touraine, around Tours, makes Vouvray and Montlouis from Chenin Blanc, dry to sweet and sparkling. Chinon, Bourgueil and Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil make Cabernet Franc reds, from light to structured. Touraine Sauvignon Blanc offers good value.

Far upstream, the Central Vineyards are nearer Burgundy than the Atlantic. Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé make crisp, mineral Sauvignon Blanc. Sancerre's soils: terres blanches, Kimmeridgian marl, for full wines; caillottes, limestone pebbles, for fresh ones; silex, flint, for smoky wines. Sancerre also makes red and rosé from Pinot Noir.
Match each wine to its grape.
The Centre and Touraine use different grapes.

Pouilly-Fumé, on the opposite bank from Sancerre, is known for flint and a smoky, gunflint character. Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly and Coteaux du Giennois make similar Sauvignon at lower prices. Don't confuse Pouilly-Fumé with Pouilly-Fuissé, a Chardonnay from Burgundy's Mâconnais.
Pouilly-Fumé and Pouilly-Fuissé are made from the same grape.
Not true. Pouilly-Fumé is Loire Sauvignon Blanc; Pouilly-Fuissé is Burgundy Chardonnay.
Touraine makes Vouvray Chenin and Chinon Cabernet Franc
Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé make mineral Sauvignon
Soils like silex and caillottes shape Sancerre
Reading the Loire and eating with it

Most Loire labels name the appellation, not the grape. Sweetness terms help for Chenin: sec, dry; demi-sec, off-dry; moelleux, sweet; doux, very sweet. Sur lie marks lees-aged Muscadet. Crémant de Loire and Saumur Brut mark traditional method sparkling wine.

Muscadet suits oysters and mussels. Sancerre suits goat's cheese, like crottin de Chavignol, and fish. Vouvray demi-sec suits pork and spicy food. Chinon suits charcuterie, rillettes and roast chicken, served slightly cool. Sweet Layon suits fruit tarts and blue cheese.
Which Loire cheese is a classic match for Sancerre?
Crottin de Chavignol is a goat's cheese from a Sancerre village.
The Loire is one of France's best sources of value. Cabernet Franc from Chinon and Muscadet sur lie offer real character at modest prices.
Order these Loire terms from driest to sweetest.
Loire labels name places; learn the grapes
Sec to doux mark Chenin's sweetness
Muscadet with oysters, Sancerre with goat's cheese
Match each area to its signature wine.
What soil gives Pouilly-Fumé its smoky character?
Saumur makes traditional method sparkling wine.
Yes, Saumur Brut, mainly from Chenin Blanc.
Muscadet aged on its lees until bottling is labelled ____ lie.
The Loire runs from maritime Nantes to continental Sancerre
